Rashi on Gittin 12a:10:1.hebrew: לא לישקל מיניה - ויהא ביד העבד, שמא יש יום שלא ימצא להשתכר:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:10:1.english: Should not take from him - and [the surplus] should remain in the slave's hand, [for] perhaps there is a day when he will not find [work] to earn [a wage].

Rashi on Gittin 12a:11:1.hebrew: וחי - כתיב ונס אל אחת הערים האל וחי:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:11:1.english: And he shall live - [The verse states]: "And he shall flee to one of these cities, and live."

Rashi on Gittin 12a:16:1.hebrew: כבודה בת מלך - כל ישראל בני מלכים:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:16:1.english: All glorious is the king's daughter - All of Israel are children of kings.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:16:2.hebrew: פנימה - צנועה, ואין דרכה לצאת ולסבב בעיר שאינה משם, ואין מכירין אותה להביא לה מלאכה בביתה, אלא אם כן מסבבת בעיר למצוא מלאכה להשתכר:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:16:2.english: Within - She is modest, and it is not her way to go out and wander about a city that is not her own, and [the residents] do not know her so as to bring her work in her home, unless she goes around the city to find work to earn a living.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:19:1.hebrew: ותסברא - דבדאמר ליה "עשה עמי" קא מיירי:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:19:1.english: And can you understand [it so]? - [Do you think] that [the dispute] is speaking about a case where he said to him, "Work with me"?

Rashi on Gittin 12a:19:2.hebrew: ועוד מאי שנא שני בצורת - אפילו בשני שובע, כיון דא"ל האדון "עשה עמי", הרי הן לו שני בצורת:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:19:2.english: And furthermore, what is different about years of famine - Even in years of plenty, once [the slave] said to [his master], "Work for me," they are for him [like] years of famine.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:20:1.english: Does not suffice - It is not sufficient.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:21:1.hebrew: מאן דמרחם אבני חרי אעבדא נמי מרחם - דשייך במצות כאשה:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:21:1.english: One who has mercy on freemen also has mercy on a slave - For [the slave] is subject to commandments, like a woman.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:22:1.hebrew: לוה ואוכל עושה ופורע - לא יעשה תחלה, דפרוטה קמייתא קדשה לה, ושוב אסור לו. אלא לוה תחילה ואוכל, ועושה פחות פחות משוה פרוטה, ופורע, כדמפרש לקמיה. וקס"ד בשאין מעלה לו מזונות, וקאמר דיכול להקדיש, אלמא יכול לומר לו: עשה עמי ואיני זנך:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:22:1.english: Borrows and eats, performs and repays - He should not work first, because the first perutah [of work] becomes consecrated, and thereafter it is forbidden for him [to work for himself]. Rather, he first borrows and eats, and then performs [work worth] less than a perutah at a time, and repays, as [the Gemara] will explain later. And the assumption [of the Gemara] is that [this is] where [the master] does not provide him with sustenance, and [Rav] says that he is able to consecrate [the slave's hands]; evidently, [a master] can say to him: "Work for me, and I will not sustain you."

Rashi on Gittin 12a:2:1.hebrew: לא תלקט לעני - סמכינהו רחמנא לשני הפסוקים: "לא תלקט", "לעני ולגר", ודרשינן סמוכין: לא תלקט אתה לצורך העני:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:2:1.english: You shall not gather for the poor - The Merciful One juxtaposed them [the phrases] "you shall not gather" and "for the poor and for the stranger," and we expound the juxtaposition [as follows]: You shall not gather, yourself, on behalf of the poor person.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:3:1.hebrew: להזהיר עני על שלו - עני הראוי ליטול פאה, ויש לו שדה, הזהירו הכתוב להניח בה פאה:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:3:1.english: To warn a poor person regarding his own - A poor person who is eligible to take pe'a, and who has a field [of his own], the verse warned him to leave pe'a in it.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:4:2.hebrew: עשה עמי - מלאכה, ואיני זנך, אלא חזור על הפתחים:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:4:2.english: Work for me - [Perform] labor, and I will not sustain you, rather go around to the doors [i.e., beg for your food].

Rashi on Gittin 12a:6:1.hebrew: בדלא ספקא - שאין מעשה ידיה מספיק לזוןה במעשה ידיה, וצריך להוסיף משלו:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:6:1.english: In a case where it does not suffice - [Where her earnings are] not enough to sustain her by her earnings, and he must add from his own.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:7:1.hebrew: ופרכינן עבד נמי לא ספק ומשני עבדא דנהום כרסיה לא שויא - עבד שאינו שוה לחם אכלו:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:7:1.english: And we ask: 'A slave also [is a case of one whose earnings] are not sufficient'; and [the Gemara] answers: 'A slave who is not worth the bread of his belly' - A slave who is not worth the bread he eats.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:7:2.hebrew: למריה למאי מתבעי - הלכך אינו מוסיף משלו, אלא יחזור על הפתחים, כי מי יכופנו לזונו ולהפסיד שלו? אבל אשה, כך התנה עמה בכתובתה: "ואת תהא יתבא בביתי ומיתזנא מנכסי":
Rashi on Gittin 12a:7:2.english: For what is he needed by his master - Therefore, [the master] does not add anything from his own, but [the slave] goes around to the doors [to beg], for who can compel [the master] to sustain him and lose his own [money]? But a wife — this is what [the husband] stipulated with her in her marriage contract: "And you shall dwell in my house and be sustained from my property."

Rashi on Gittin 12a:8:1.hebrew: שגלה לערי מקלט - שהרג בשוגג, וגלה:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:8:1.english: Who was exiled to the cities of refuge - Who killed unintentionally and was exiled.

Rashi on Gittin 12a:9:1.hebrew: להעדפה - שמעשה ידיו עודפים על מזונותיו:
Rashi on Gittin 12a:9:1.english: For the surplus - For the work of his hands exceeds his sustenance.

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:11:1.hebrew: מאי שנא לערי מקלט - פי' אי אמרת בשלמא יכול אשמועינן ערי מקלט, דאע"ג דאמר רחמנא וחי עביד ליה חיותא טפי, אפי' הכי יכול הרב לומר כו'. אבל לענין העדפה לא משמע ליה דמשום וחי תיהוי העדפה דידיה:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:11:1.english: "And what is different with regard to cities of refuge?" - Explanation: Granted, if you say that [the baraita] teaches "he can" [say this] with regard to cities of refuge — that although the Merciful One said "and he shall live," [implying that] one should provide him with extra sustenance, even so the master can say, etc. But with regard to the surplus, [the Gemara] does not mean [to say] that because of "and he shall live" the surplus should be his.

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:16:1.hebrew: מספקת מאי למימרא כו' - אי אמרת בשלמא כולה בדספקא תנא, סיפא דאמר לה — לגלויי ארישא דאיירי בלא אמר לה; אבל השתא דמוקמת רישא בדלא ספקא, ולא תנא הך סיפא אלא לאשמועינן דבמספקת יכול לומר לה: "צאי מעשה ידיך במזונותיך" — מאי למימרא? דזה אינו שום חידוש:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:16:1.english: "[If her earnings] suffice, what is [the Gemara] saying [i.e., what is the point]?" etc. - If you were to say, granted, that the entire [baraita] teaches [a case] of insufficient [earnings], then the latter clause, which says [that the husband] "said to her" [that she may support herself from her earnings], serves to reveal about the first clause that it is speaking of a case where he did not say this to her. But now that you establish the first clause as [dealing with a case where her earnings are] not insufficient, and [the baraita] teaches this latter clause only to inform us that where [her earnings] suffice he can say to her, "Go out and [use] the work of your hands for your sustenance" — what is the point of stating this? For this is no novelty at all:

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:18:1.hebrew: ומר סבר אינו יכול - והא דקתני "או הוציאני לחירות" — לאו דוקא, אלא כלומר: שיהיה מעשה ידי לעצמי, כמו לבן חורין:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:18:1.english: And one Sage holds that he cannot - And as for what [the Gemara] taught, "or release me to freedom" — it is not precise, but rather it means: that the work of my hands will be for myself, like a free person:

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:1:1.hebrew: דילמא לא היא - דחויא בעלמא היא, דרב פפא אית ליה בהדיא: תופס לב"ת במקום שחב לאחרים לא קנה (כתובות דף פד:):
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:1:1.english: Perhaps it is not so - It is merely a [weak] rebuttal, for Rav Papa has an explicit [ruling]: One who seizes [property] on behalf of a creditor, in a case where this harms others, has not acquired [it] (Ketubot 84b):

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:21:1.hebrew: כי היכי דחזו אינשי ומרחמי - הקשה ה"ר יצחק בן הר"מ: דבפרק השולח (לקמן גיטין דף לז:) גבי עבד שנשבה ופדאו ישראל אחר, שמעינן להו איפכא! דקא אמרי רבנן: לא ישתעבד, לא לרבו ראשון ולא לרבו שני. לרבו שני לא, דהא לשם בן חורין פרקיה; לרבו ראשון לא, דלמא מימנעי ולא פרקי. ורשב"ג סבר: כשם שמצוה לפדות בני חורין, כן מצוה לפדות את העבדים. ואומר ר"י דרבן שמעון ב"ג סבר דלענין פדיון פרקי ליה טפי, שלא יטמע בין העובדי כוכבים; ורבנן סברי דלענין מזונות מרחמי עליה טפי, שלא ימות ברעב, וגם כל א' יתן לו מעט לחם, אבל בפדיון צריך הרבה ביחד:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:21:1.english: "So that people will see and have mercy" - Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Meir raised a difficulty: In the chapter [beginning] "HaShole'ach" (below, Gittin 37b), regarding a slave who was captured and another Jew redeemed him, we find the opposite of this! For the Rabbis say: He shall not be subjugated, neither to his first master nor to his second master. To his second master, no, for he redeemed him for the sake of a freeman; to his first master, no, lest people refrain and not redeem [slaves]. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds: Just as it is a mitzvah to redeem freemen, so it is a mitzvah to redeem slaves. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that with regard to redemption, people will redeem him more, so that he not be absorbed among the idolaters; and the Rabbis hold that with regard to sustenance, people will have mercy on him more, so that he not die of hunger, and also each one will give him a little bread, but for redemption a large amount is needed all at once:

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:22:1.hebrew: אמר רב המקדיש ידי עבדו - גרסינן. ולא גרסינן "המקדיש עבדו", דהתם יצא לחירות, כדאמר רב בהשולח (לקמן גיטין דף לח:), דליהוי עם קדוש קאמר. וא"ת: וכי היכי דמקדיש ידי עבדו אמרינן דהן קדושים למלאכתן, הכי נמי כשהקדיש כל עבדו הוה לן למימר שהקדישו למלאכתו — פיו לדבורו, ידיו למעשהו, רגליו להילוכו, דבענין זה חשיב הקדש, כדאמרינן בסוף פ"ק דנדרים (דף יג:). ואומר רבי' יצחק דסברא הוא דלא נתכוין להקדישו למלאכתו, לפי שיש חילוק במלאכתו, שאין פיו ידיו ורגליו שוין במלאכתן; הלכך אית לן למימר דלשחררו נתכוין, דהוי הכל בענין אחד. אי נמי י"ל: התם כשמקדיש עבדו סתם, משמע יותר למיהוי עם קדוש, דהא למלאכתו לא קאמר; אבל מקדיש ידי עבדו, הקדיש מלאכת ידיו, דלא שייך למימר בענין אחר:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:22:1.english: "Rav said: One who consecrates the hands of his slave" - This is our reading. And we do not read "one who consecrates his slave," for there [in that case] he goes out to freedom, as Rav said in [the chapter] Hashole'ach (below, Gittin 38b), that he meant [that the slave should become] a holy people. And if you ask: Just as when one consecrates the hands of his slave we say that they are holy for their labor, so too when he consecrated his entire slave we should have said that he consecrated him for his labor — his mouth for his speech, his hands for his work, his feet for his walking, for in this manner it is considered consecration, as we say at the end of the first chapter of Nedarim (13b)? And our Rabbi Yitzchak says: It is logical that he did not intend to consecrate him for his labor, because there is a difference in his labor, as his mouth, hands, and feet are not equal in their labor; therefore we must say that he intended to free him, since [then] everything is in one manner. Alternatively, one can say: There, when he consecrates his slave without specification, it implies more that [the slave] should be a holy people, since he did not say [that it is] for his labor; but [when he] consecrates the hands of his slave, he has consecrated the work of his hands, for it is not possible to say [that he meant it] in another manner:

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:2:1.hebrew: אלא דכתיב לא תלקט לעני - וא"ת: למ"ד בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ד:) כל מילתא דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד, אי עביד — מהני, א"כ קנה העני? וי"ל: דהכא בתר "לא תלקט" כתיב "לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם", משמע דלא קני. וא"ת: ונילף מהכא בעלמא, דהמגביה מציאה לחבירו דלא קנה חבירו? וי"ל: דהכא סברא הוא, שלא זכתה תורה לעני אלא מה שכל אחד מלקט לצורך עצמו. ולרב חסדא דמפרש הכא דטעמייהו דרבנן משום דתופס לב"ח לא קני, איכא למימר דמהכא יליף:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:2:1.english: "Rather, as it is written: 'You shall not gather for the poor'" - And if you ask: According to the one who says in the first chapter of Temurah (4b) that anything the Merciful One said not to do, if one did it, it is effective — then [in that case] the poor person should have acquired [the produce]? And one can answer: Here, after "you shall not gather," it is written "for the poor and the convert you shall leave them," which implies that he does not acquire. And if you ask: Let us derive from here in general that one who lifts up a found object for his fellow, his fellow does not acquire it? And one can answer: Here it is [based on] logic, that the Torah granted the poor person only what each person gathers for his own needs. And according to Rav Chisda, who explains here that the reason of the Rabbis is because one who seizes [property] for a creditor does not effect acquisition, one can say that he derives [it] from here.

Tosafot on Gittin 12a:7:1.hebrew: עבד נמי בדלא ספיק - וא"ת: אטו משום דלא ספיק יהא רבו חייב לזונו, ולא יוכל לומר לו "צא מעשה ידיך במזונותיך"? ועוד קשה הלשון דקאמר "עבדא דנהום כריסיה לא שוי"; הוה ליה למימר בהדיא דלא מחייב לזונו, כיון דאמר ליה "צא מעשה ידיך במזונותיך". ואור"י דס"ד דרגילות הוא שעבד עצמו הולך ועובד את רבו, אפילו כשאמר ליה "צא מעשה ידיך במזונותיך". משום הכי בעי למימר (אע"ג) דלא ספיק שיתחייב במזונות, כיון שמ"מ עובדו. משום הכי מהדר ליה בלשון זה: "עבדא דנהום כריסיה לא שוי" כו'. ולהכי קאמר לעיל "ש"מ יכול הרב לומר לעבד: עשה עמי ואיני זנך", דאפי' מיירי דא"ל "צא מעשה ידיך במזונותיך", מ"מ כיון שעובדו היה לו להתחייב במזונותיו, אי לאו משום דיכול. ועוד דסלקא דעתיה דמיירי בלא אמר ליה, דומיא דאשה דבדלא ספיק לא שכיח:
Tosafot on Gittin 12a:7:1.english: "A slave also, [in a case where] he does not suffice" - And if you ask: Is it because he does not suffice [for his own sustenance] that his master should be obligated to feed him, and [the master] could not say to him, "Go out; [live from] the work of your hands for your sustenance"? Furthermore, the wording is difficult, for [the Gemara] says, "A slave who is not worth the bread he consumes"; it should have said explicitly that [the master] is not obligated to feed him, since he said to him, "Go out; [live from] the work of your hands for your sustenance." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak answered that the [Gemara] thought that it is customary that a slave goes on his own and works for his master, even when [the master] said to him, "Go out; [live from] the work of your hands for your sustenance." Therefore [the Gemara] wanted to say [that] even though he does not suffice, [the master] should be obligated in his sustenance, since in any case he works for him. Therefore [the Gemara] answers him with this wording: "A slave who is not worth the bread he consumes," etc. And that is why [the Gemara] said earlier, "Learn from this that a master can say to a slave: Work with me, and I will not feed you," for even if [the mishnah] is speaking of where he said to him, "Go out; [live from] the work of your hands for your sustenance," nevertheless, since [the slave] works for him, [the master] should have been obligated in his sustenance, were it not that he is able [to refuse]. Furthermore, it entered [the Gemara's] mind that [the mishnah] is speaking of a case where he did not say this to him, similar to a woman, where [a case of] not sufficing is uncommon:
